description: Stock-style photograph of a row of American houses with wraparound porches, each flying a large U.S. flag from an angled porch-mounted flagpole. Manicured lawns, trimmed shrubs, porch steps with railings, and a lamppost line the street; a stone building stands in the background. Filed in the archive as 'Love of Country.jpg' and used with multiple Q drops as a patriotic image; no text or identifiable location appears.
flags: Location not identifiable; generic stock-style Americana image

description: Dark-theme screenshot of a Q drop that attaches a three-photo collage and questions whether the Jussie Smollett case was a 'false flag' tied to the Senate anti-lynching bill. The collage shows Smollett posing with Barack and Michelle Obama at what appears to be a White House event, a street-march photo including Rep. Maxine Waters, and Smollett with a woman consistent with Rep. Sheila Jackson Lee and another man. The drop links a Fox News article on Cory Booker and asks a series of rhetorical questions about Kamala Harris, Booker, Chicago PD, and Rahm Emanuel, ending '#WakeUpAmerica'.

description: Extremely tall screenshot of a Bing news search results page, archived under the filename '7day BING QAnon search results.png' — apparently the past 7 days of news coverage mentioning QAnon (circa late March 2019, around the Mueller report's delivery). It shows on the order of 80-100 stacked result rows, each with a small thumbnail, headline, outlet name, and timestamp, from many different outlets; visible thumbnails include cable-news stills, social-media logos, and a large Q graphic. The image is rendered at very low resolution and the headline text is too small to read reliably.
flags: FLAGGED FOR MANUAL REVIEW: dozens of headline rows are illegible at the available resolution — individual headlines, outlets, and dates could not be transcribed
Interpretation as a 7-day 'QAnon' Bing news search comes from the archived filename and page layout, not from readable on-image text
